packages.title: DESNZ local and regional GHG scope QA
facts: DESNZ publishes local authority and regional greenhouse-gas estimates for the UK.
The series uses nationally available datasets and provides a consistent breakdown going back to 2005.
The local and regional series covers territorial carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide.
Fluorinated gases are not included in the local and regional series and are instead included in UK territorial greenhouse-gas statistics.
Local-authority estimates are not direct measurements for individual cadastral parcels.

packages.title: Local inventory indicator boundary QA
facts: DESNZ describes the local and regional series as the most reliable and consistent breakdown available across the country.
The estimates are intended to support local and regional indicators and inventories.
The series is territorial rather than consumption-based or residence-based.
A local-authority inventory does not establish facility-specific or property-specific emissions without additional evidence.
Geographic scope must be preserved when using the series for comparison or screening.

packages.title: DESNZ hydrogen production and demand 2022 to 2025 QA
facts: DESNZ published a June 2026 Energy Trends special feature on hydrogen production and demand in the UK.
The feature covers the period 2022 to 2025.
The article was first published on 30 June 2026.
Supporting data tables were added on 6 July 2026.
Hydrogen production and demand quantities are not automatically greenhouse-gas intensity measurements.

packages.title: Hydrogen series publication-vintage QA
facts: The hydrogen feature belongs to the June 2026 Energy Trends publication cycle.
The underlying reference period ends in 2025 rather than 2026.
Publication date and reference period must remain separate metadata fields.
Production and demand statistics require an explicit emissions methodology before they can support GHG calculations.
No parcel-level hydrogen-related emissions value is inferred from national production or demand statistics.

packages.title: Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard version 4 QA
facts: The UK Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard version 4 was published for January 2026.
Version 4 updates emissions factors, technical parameters and calculation methodologies in its data annex.
Version 4 expands biomethane eligibility to include gas-grid sourcing under a mass-balance approach.
Version 4 introduces updated evidence requirements relating to Renewable Energy Guarantees of Origin.
The applicable standard version must be preserved for any compliance assessment.

packages.title: Hydrogen emissions calculator boundary QA
facts: DESNZ provides a Hydrogen Emissions Calculator for use with the Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard.
The calculator is intended to estimate greenhouse-gas emissions associated with a prospective hydrogen production facility for likely compliance assessment.
The calculator output is a calculated compliance input rather than a direct observation of actual facility emissions.
The full calculator was revised on 5 February 2026 to address a minor formula error affecting dashboard calculations.
Calculated prospective facility results must not be relabelled as measured parcel emissions.

packages.title: NSTA carbon-storage-complex geometry QA
facts: The NSTA dataset maps current UK Continental Shelf carbon storage complexes.
The dataset describes carbon capture and storage as capture of CO2 followed by transport and underground storage.
The dataset notes that stored CO2 is typically placed at depths greater than 800 metres where it behaves as a supercritical fluid.
The storage-complex dataset was updated in June 2026 and is available in multiple geospatial formats.
Storage-complex geometry does not itself measure the quantity of CO2 captured or stored by a specific industrial site.

packages.title: CCS geospatial data versus emissions QA
facts: NSTA provides the storage-complex data in formats including GeoJSON, KML, CSV and geodatabase resources.
The dataset concerns offshore geological storage areas rather than emissions-source parcels.
Industrial processes such as steel, cement, hydrogen production and power generation are examples of potential CO2 capture sources described in the dataset summary.
A mapped storage complex must not be treated as proof that a particular facility is connected to or using that complex.
No captured-emissions quantity is inferred from storage-area geometry alone.

packages.title: Environment Agency Pollution Inventory release scope QA
facts: The Environment Agency Pollution Inventory collates annual mass releases of specified substances from regulated industrial sites.
It includes releases to air, controlled waters and sewers.
It also records quantities of waste transferred off site.
The current National Data Library page provides downloadable annual resources covering 2013 to 2024.
Pollution Inventory facility records must remain distinct from cadastral parcel records.

packages.title: Pollution Inventory permit-scope QA
facts: Pollution Inventory reporting covers the whole regulated authorisation or permit.
The reporting scope includes non-point and fugitive emissions such as leaks.
The reporting scope also includes specific point sources such as chimneys.
Large industrial sites regulated under the environmental permitting framework report annual releases of listed substances.
A facility-wide reported release must not be assigned to an individual land parcel without a verified facility-to-parcel relationship.

packages.title: DESNZ industrial technical research scope QA
facts: DESNZ published its Industrial technical research collection in July 2026.
The collection includes research on industrial fuel switching and electrification.
It includes industrial resource and energy efficiency and carbon capture utilisation and storage.
It also includes Direct Air Capture, bioenergy with CCS, life-cycle assessment and anaerobic digestion research.
Research outputs must be distinguished from operational facility measurements and official statistical inventories.

packages.title: Industrial research evidence-use QA
facts: DESNZ states that the collection contains technical research commissioned from external organisations.
The reports use a mix of quantitative and qualitative methods.
The purpose is to collate synthesise and analyse evidence for policy and stakeholders.
A technical research result may provide methodology or evidence context without being a direct measurement for a target parcel.
Any numerical research result must retain its study boundary method and source before reuse.

packages.title: Defra UK consumption carbon footprint 2023 QA
facts: Defra reports the UK consumption-based greenhouse-gas footprint at an estimated 699 MtCO2e in 2023.
The 2023 footprint was reported as 4 percent lower than in 2022.
The 2023 footprint remained below the 2007 peak of 984 MtCO2e.
The measure is consumption-based and therefore differs from territorial and residence-basis emissions.
A national consumption footprint must not be assigned to individual parcels or facilities.

packages.title: Defra carbon-footprint revision QA
facts: The carbon-footprint release was updated on 24 July 2026 with a correction to geographical coverage in an England dataset table.
A separate correction on 7 July 2026 amended text describing emissions associated with imports from the EU.
Defra reports that carbon dioxide represented 78 percent of the UK consumption-based GHG total in 2023.
Defra reports carbon dioxide represented 79 percent of England's consumption-based GHG total in 2023.
Corrections and revision dates must be retained when using the footprint series.

packages.title: DESNZ greenhouse-gas conversion factors 2026 QA
facts: DESNZ published greenhouse-gas reporting conversion factors for 2026 on 11 June 2026.
The factors are intended to help users calculate and report greenhouse-gas emissions from UK activities in 2026.
DESNZ provides a full spreadsheet set and a flat file intended for automatic processing.
DESNZ also provides a methodology document and a major-changes document.
Conversion factors are calculation inputs and are not direct observations of emissions at a parcel.

packages.title: Activity-based versus spend-based factor QA
facts: DESNZ distinguishes its activity-based conversion factors from Defra spend-based emissions multipliers.
Defra spend-based multipliers are primarily intended to compare carbon intensities of categories of final UK demand.
Spend-based methods may be used for an initial supply-chain assessment where sufficient activity data are unavailable.
DESNZ advises users to report the methods used for their emissions accounting.
A calculated estimate must retain the factor version and method rather than being labelled as a direct measurement.

packages.title: DESNZ heat-pump deployment March 2026 QA
facts: DESNZ published Heat pump deployment statistics for March 2026 on 11 June 2026.
The series monitors hydronic heat pumps with capacity up to 45 kW installed in the UK.
The scope includes air-source and ground-source heat pumps.
The statistics are published as official statistics in development and may be revised.
Installation counts are deployment activity data rather than direct greenhouse-gas measurements.

packages.title: Heat-pump deployment versus GHG QA
facts: Heat-pump deployment statistics count installations rather than avoided greenhouse-gas emissions.
The series is intended to monitor deployment levels and support methodological development.
Its provisional status requires future revisions to be preserved.
Technology deployment does not establish the energy consumption or operating emissions of an individual property.
No parcel carbon value is inferred from a heat-pump installation count alone.

packages.title: Heat Networks Planning Database project-stage QA
facts: The DESNZ Heat Networks Planning Database covers district and communal heat-network deployment across the UK.
The database tracks project stages including inception, planning, construction, operation and decommissioning.
The data are sourced from review of planning applications and contact with developers.
The database is updated during the month following the end of each quarter.
Project stage does not by itself establish heat delivered or greenhouse-gas emissions avoided.

packages.title: Heat Networks Planning Database quarter-vintage QA
facts: The National Data Library Heat Networks Planning Database page was updated on 3 July 2026.
The page provides a February 2026 to April 2026 project dataset.
CSV and spreadsheet resources for that period were added in June 2026.
Quarterly project-pipeline data must retain project stage and observation period.
A planning or operational status must not be converted to a parcel emissions value without explicit measurement evidence.
